name: Immutable local validation permit
purpose: Model the immutable, host-issued permit that binds exactly one session identity and its full operational envelope, with a stable content identity and a closed allowed-action set.
responsibilities: Bind exactly one session identity, plan digest, scenario, deployment, environment, tool, interface, target, nonce, validity interval (with a declared clock domain), and a bounded list of finite quotas.
Remain immutable after construction: no mutator is exposed and all fields are comparable for equality.
Reject at construction any absent/default identity-bearing field, any undefined action bit, any composite action mask not explicitly allowed, and any unknown quota kind.
Compute a deterministic PermitId as the FNV-1a 128-bit digest of the canonical serialization of all bound fields, including the nonce.
Expose the allowed action set as a bounded list of explicitly allowed action masks for exact-membership validation.
state_ownership: A permit is an immutable value object; a built permit never changes. The builder owns transient validation state until the permit is finalized.
interfaces: PermitBuilder: set_<field>(...) -> Result; build(Permit& out) -> Result
Permit: const accessors for each bound field; permit_id(); allowed_actions(); equality comparison
SessionContext: the runtime-envelope claim compared field-by-field against a permit at consumption
concurrency: Permits are immutable values and may be shared and copied across threads without synchronization; builders are single-threaded by construction.
errors: InvalidPermit (with FieldLocator): missing/default identity field, undefined action bit, non-explicit composite mask, unknown quota kind, or out-of-bounds value at construction.
deployment: Header/source pair in the standalone candidate; bounded fixed-size arrays carry tags, digests, and quotas so no unbounded allocation occurs.
rationale: Immutability plus content identity make exactly-once consumption and replay detection sound: any field change (including a changed nonce) yields a different identity, while the bound session identity is still checked against the consumed-session set.
